job.title: Senior IT Project Manager - Data & Analytics Architecture and Reporting
job.description:
Duration: 6 months to start

Job Description
  • This is a delivery-ownership and program-control role, not a passive coordination or status-reporting role.
  • The Sr. IT Project Manager is accountable for maintaining the integrated plan, running the operating cadence, driving action completion, managing risks and dependencies, producing clear documentation, and escalating issues before they affect committed milestones.
  • The Sr. IT Project Manager owns the Interim Data Architecture and Wave 1 Reporting project end to end: the integrated plan, the critical path, a dozen cross-functional dependencies, and the decisions on KPI definitions and hierarchy mappings that determine whether the reports land on time and mean the same thing to both companies.
  • The hardest part of this project is not moving data — it is getting two organizations to agree on what a metric means, how a hierarchy rolls up, and who has final say. You will drive that.
  • You will partner daily with the Business Product Manager (the single accountable business voice for scope and acceptance), data architecture and engineering leads, security and compliance, vendor delivery teams, and regional business leads, and you will present regularly to IT leadership and executive sponsors.
  • The successful candidate must be able to operate independently with limited day-to-day direction.
  • This person will establish and run the workstream operating cadence, require timely updates from workstream owners, follow up on overdue actions, facilitate resolution of cross-functional blockers, and escalate missed commitments with a recommended path forward.
  • The role reports to the Senior Program Manager, Technology IMO/PMO, and is a contract engagement of approximately 9–10 months with strong potential for extension into Wave 2.
Core Responsibilities
  • Delivery Leadership: Own the end-to-end plan from mobilization through Wave 1 release — infrastructure, network, security, and IAM pre-requisites; data platform and architecture enablement; master data cross-mapping; pilot execution; and report delivery. Baseline it in the first 30 days and hold the team to it.
  • Report Readiness and Release Management: Establish and track entry and exit criteria for each report migration. Coordinate data validation, reconciliation, technical testing, business UAT, defect resolution, business acceptance, deployment readiness, cutover, hypercare, and transition to ongoing support. Maintain a report-level readiness view that clearly shows what is on track, at risk, blocked, or ready for release.
  • Critical Path Ownership: Own the critical path from the Day 1 hard dependency through build start and every report release. Know at all times what is on it, what threatens it, and what you are doing about it.
  • Dependency Management: Drive and unblock dependencies across Cloud Infrastructure, Network, Enterprise Platform, DevOps, Cyber, Legal, and Compliance (SOX/GxP). Track ERP (ECC/S/4) interdependencies that can force pipeline rework and get ahead of them.
  • Decision Facilitation: Run the KPI definition and hierarchy-mapping decision process so that the same label carries the same rules, inclusions, units, and calculation timing in both companies. Resolve the 4-4-5 vs. Gregorian calendar and close/forecast rhythm mismatches report by report. Force decisions; do not wait for consensus to arrive.
  • Scope Control: Defend the P1/P2 boundary. Route every new request to Wave 2 through change control and make the trade-off visible to sponsors.
  • Team Coordination and Accountability: Direct day-to-day delivery across vendor teams and internal SMEs from both companies. Maintain a clear action tracker with one accountable owner and due date for every action. Secure updates, follow up on missed commitments, identify resource and capacity gaps early, and escalate unresolved items before they become schedule slips.
  • Risk, Issue, Action, Dependency, and Decision Management: Own the integrated RAID, action, dependency, assumption, and decision logs. Ensure each item has a clear owner, target date, impact, mitigation or resolution path, and escalation status. Review open items routinely, drive closure, and escalate early with a recommendation and clear decision required.
  • Governance, Status, and Executive Reporting: Establish and maintain the weekly workstream status cadence and monthly executive reporting process. Produce accurate, concise, decision-oriented status materials covering milestone progress, critical-path health, accomplishments, upcoming work, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions needed, overdue actions, resource concerns, and recovery plans. Ensure materials are distributed on time and require minimal revision from leadership. Operate within IT governance and change-control standards.
  • Program Documentation and Information Management: Create and maintain the core program documentation, including the integrated plan, milestone baseline, action tracker, dependency map, RAID log, decision log, change log, meeting agendas, meeting records, executive briefings, and report readiness dashboard. Convert complex discussions into clear decisions, actions, owners, and dates. Maintain a reliable single source of truth with consistent version control and easy access for stakeholders.
  • First 30 Days: Baseline the integrated plan, confirm scope and milestones, establish the weekly status and action-management cadence, validate workstream ownership, create the initial RAID and dependency views, identify critical-path threats, and recommend immediate recovery actions for any areas already at risk.
Required Qualifications
  • Experience: 10+ years of IT project management, including 4+ years leading data platform, BI, or analytics programs in a large global enterprise.
  • M&A Delivery: Hands-on delivery experience on an M&A integration, carve-out, or separation. You understand Day 1 hard dependencies, TSA-era constraints, and how decisions actually get made when two companies share a table.
  • Track Record: Demonstrated delivery of large, multi-team, multi-region technology projects to a fixed, business-committed date — with examples of how you recovered when the plan broke.
  • Technical Fluency: Working command of modern data architecture — cloud lakehouse platforms (Snowflake and/or Databricks), BI tooling, data pipelines, master data management, and data governance — deep enough to challenge an engineer's estimate and be right.
  • Master Data: Direct experience harmonizing master data and hierarchies (product, customer, vendor, material) across systems or companies, including the business negotiation that comes with it.
  • Compliance: Working familiarity with SOX (ideally GxP) control environments and security/IAM review gates, and experience building compliance evidence into the delivery plan rather than bolting it on.
  • Executive Presence: Comfortable presenting to VP and C-level sponsors, taking a hard question, and running a decision meeting with regional leads who disagree — and driving it to closure in the room.
  • Program Operating Discipline: Demonstrated ability to independently run a complex program operating cadence, manage competing priorities, drive action completion across teams without direct authority, maintain highly organized records, and escalate missed commitments appropriately. Must be known for strong follow-through, attention to detail, and producing clear, executive-ready documents.
  • Program Management Tools and Documentation: Expert in Microsoft Project or equivalent, Excel, PowerPoint, and common collaboration and document-management tools such as Microsoft Teams and SharePoint. Comfortable in Smartsheet or Jira. Able to build clear, professional status reports, executive scorecards, action trackers, decision logs, and program dashboards.
Preferred Skills
  • Industry: CPG or manufacturing background.
  • Domain Reporting: Familiarity with daily sales, market share, secondary sales, eCommerce POS, spend analytics, supply chain finance, and capital planning reporting.
  • PMO Experience: Prior work inside an IMO/PMO or SPMO structure with capital governance and business-case review processes.
  • ERP Exposure: SAP ECC/S/4 exposure from an analytics-consumer perspective.
  • Operating Style: Thrives in ambiguity and shifting priorities in a fast-paced, global, matrixed environment. Brings structure without waiting for direction, creates practical operating rhythms, follows through persistently with stakeholders, and gives leaders early visibility into risks, missed commitments, and decisions required.

Duration: 8 months to start 

Position Summary:
Under the general supervision of the Technical Services Supervisor & Radio Coordinator, this position provides specialized technical and comprehensive support, consultation, and training services for Department staff on P25 digital trunking radio systems.
  • The primary responsibility and expertise are to support, configure, maintain, and install radio systems and the encompassing technologies. 
  • This position will assist in developing, recommending, and implementing standards for radio systems within all institutions (adult institutions, correctional centers and juvenile institutions) included but not limited to hardware, software and network standards for these systems.
  • The position will assist in managing radio systems including fleet mapping, maintenance and audit of Code Plug data for programmable radios, maintaining inventory of radio equipment, coordinating purchase of equipment to ensure compatibility and cost effectiveness, coordinate with outside agencies interoperability of radio equipment and frequencies, assist purchasing agent in development of requests for purchase for radio systems and equipment, and assist in administration of FCC frequencies licensed to the client.
  • This position will assist in connecting these systems to existing state networks and stay up to date with networking & I.T. principles in line with Wisconsin BTM.  Extensive field work and travel are incorporated in this position with "hands on" work in installing and maintaining these systems. 
  • This position will work closely with the client and other facilities, Department facilities management, and vendors in lifecycle management of radio-based systems. 
  • The person assigned to this position will be required to assist in directing vendors in installation and maintenance of these systems.
 
This position shall comply with the Department’s administrative rules and the agency’s policies and procedures including those related to the Department's overall Reentry philosophy of using evidence-based strategies, practices and programs which target an offender’s individual criminogenic needs and risk level.

Goals and Work Activities:
Analysis and review to ensure compliance for new and existing radio systems
  • Analyze performance data related to radio systems with the development of techniques to optimize the use of radio resources.  Assist and advise institutions and centers on providing the necessary data to account for their radio communications needs for the upcoming biennium and provide recommendations on improvements to their plans and implementation strategies.
  • Assist with the development of department radio communications planning for the better use of existing services and consideration of new services and technologies.
  • Assist with standardization of operating procedures for all institutions and centers to follow.  This would include a Communications Plan, Security Internal Management Procedures (SIMPs), policies and procedures as required by Security and Internal management, and establishing disaster recovery plans and services.
  • Assist with securing and administering FCC radio frequency licenses including filing applications with the FCC on a timely basis, with necessary input from the installation vendors, to ensure that the systems can be operational when needed.
  • Assist with maintaining Tower Licenses and FAA approval for towers located near airports.  
  • Coordinate with outside agencies the analysis of frequency use for Mutual Aide and Emergency response.  Assist with developing Memorandums of Understanding for authorized use of such frequencies or written authorization to apply for licenses for said use when appropriate.  Attend Emergency Response meetings and apply findings to radio systems.
  • Partner with vendors to build relationships, analyze processes and technology to ensure system aligns with industry standards in all areas of radio technology, including but not limited to, network, PC & cabling standards.

Assist with development and installation of radio communications systems for the department on a state-wide basis
  • Assist the installation and implementation of all new services and systems with the involved vendors, contractors, architects, engineers, departmental users and other agencies, ensuring that installations meet all client and state standards.
  • Assist in implementation of radio installs with regards to network connectivity and ensuring all systems are consistent with BTM standards.
  • Provide consultation at the appropriate office, unit, institution, division or department level on the acquisition of new radio communication systems, both under current consideration and for budgetary purposes.
  • Assist in planning and conducting reviews of service levels and equipment performance to make recommendations for the improvement of efficiencies and cost controls, responding to program changes and user needs. 
  • Assist in implementing and ensuring quality control of Fleet Map – identification of all radios, talk groups available and identification of which radios have access to specific talk groups. 
  • Assist in maintaining inventory & databases reflecting the Fleet Map and inventory of all radio
    equipment.  Maintain drawings of connectivity & key hardware items with regards to the radio systems. 
  • Maintain inventory of all Code Plugs (electronic file that contains features and programming for a specific radio) for programmable radio in the fleet.  Conduct periodic onsite analysis of radio programming of fleet radios and compare to code plug date on file to assure standardization and reliability. 
  • Assist configuring networking equipment to include switches and other network apparatus used in radio systems and connectivity to existing state networks. 
  • Install, configure and backup workstations used in any IT-integrated facility-based radio systems.

Assist with on-site radio asset management
  • Assist with the scheduling, planning and implementation of site surveys to review existing radio communication systems and services aimed at identifying problems and needs for recommending changes either in current operations, for budgetary purposes or to effectively communicate in emergency situations.
  • Assist as point of contact for emergency back-up resources in event of a systems failure.   
  • Assist with analyzing and evaluating all institution and center’s Communication Trunking System,
    a computerized frequency management system that handles multiple frequencies. Assist in maintaining consistent talk groups within the department. 

Provision of consultation and technical assistance for all radio communications systems and equipment, department-wide
  • Maintain a working knowledge of radio communications systems, services, and equipment to provide consulting service and recommendations to all department users and facilities. 
  • Establish and maintain a professional working relationship with other industry professional, vendors, equipment manufacturers and service providers to stay abreast of current and emerging technologies. 
  • Assist with studies (feasibility studies, cost benefit analysis etc.) on radio systems, equipment and services for divisional and departmental budget planning. 
  • Respond to requests for information and advice by providing technical expertise on radio communication operations, services and equipment. 
  • Assist with preparation of formal project reports, respond to questionnaires and surveys as assigned or requested and present progress to management, key stakeholders.
  • Act as liaison between department users and vendor/service providers in all areas of radio communications.
  • Assist in providing standards and other guidance material to assist institutions and offices of the department in establishing disaster recovery plans and services.
  • Communicate and assist Purchasing agent in the development of Request for Purchase for radio equipment and systems. 

Interchange of information beneficial to the department
  • Maintain liaison with other agencies to share information on common problems and to take advantage of available expertise.
  • Train Institution staff on Radio Systems.
  • Direct and in some cases develop the training plans and supervise the delivery of training to departmental employees on the use of radio communications equipment and services to assure consistency to all institutions and centers.
                                               
Professional development and other duties
  • Attend appropriate training, conferences, seminars and read technical publications to maintain a high level of expertise concerning radio communication technologies. 
  • Follow industry publications and other sources to stay abreast of industry changes and new directions within this industry.
  • Attend product demonstrations to become familiar with new hardware and software developments.
  • Share technical skills and knowledge with other staff.
  • Provide backup support to the FIIT group.
  • Provide and coordinate for the providing of training assistance for maintenance technicians.           

Job Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
  • Knowledge of radio equipment and digital radio trunking systems.
  • Knowledge of all operation procedures in radio equipment.
  • Knowledge of SIMPs.
  • Knowledge of FCC Licensing procedures and license maintenance requirements.
  • Knowledge of Radio Programming related to software and interface equipment.
  • Knowledge of how to properly maintain fleet of portable batteries.
  • Working knowledge of PCs, standard Windows OS’s and Microsoft Office (Access, Outlook, Word, Excel).  Experience with workstation backup principles.
  • Experience with networking concepts and principles.  Experience working with network hardware including switches, routers & firewalls. 
  • Experience cabling network-attached equipment, to include copper and fiber optic technologies.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Skill in resolution of conflicts of both technical issues and interpersonal relationships.
  • Skill in establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with Division personnel, institution personnel, professional consultants, vendors / trades people, and representatives of other agencies. 
  • Ability to create clear and comprehensive technical documentation and detailed system diagrams.
  • Ability to work well alone or in a team environment.
  • Ability to manage time and juggle multiple simultaneous projects and operational responsibilities.

job.title: RHTP State EHR Project Manager
job.description:
Duration: 12 months to start 

General Statement of Duties:
Serve as project manager for the Rural Health Transformation Project's Health IT initiative, specifically overseeing the planning and implementation of a State-sponsored Electronic Health Record solution. This position will be responsible for coordinating all contracted vendor activities for this project to a high degree of technical complexity.

Supervision:
Work under the direction and guidance of the State Health IT Coordinator and/or other senior program and policy leadership with considerable latitude for the exercise of initiative and independent judgment in the utilization for professional standards and techniques. 

Supervision Exercised:
No direct personnel supervised. Oversight of high-value contracts, ensuring milestones and deliverables are produced professionally and in a timely manner.

Scope of Work
  • A cornerstone of the Rural Health Transformation Project will be a state-sponsored electronic health record (EHR) solution option that meets the needs of rural providers. By aggregating demand across multiple rural practices, the State can negotiate substantially reduced per-user costs, leveraging volume discounts unavailable to individual practices.
  • This model is widely utilized by large health systems and health center associations to drive down costs for smaller, associated and independent practices, and the State is positioned to mimic this model to great effect, creating efficiencies through voluntary participation in a centralized software solution.
  • The State – or a contracted vendor – would be responsible for the complex technical and compliance aspects of EHR selection, contracting, and ongoing management. This includes ensuring the system meets all federal meaningful use requirements, HIPAA security standards, and state-specific reporting mandates.
  • The system will be pre-configured with necessary reporting feeds to the RI Department of Health, participating health plans, and the State’s Health Information Exchange.
  • Given the complexity of any EHR implementation and the complexity of the necessary legal framework and financial sustainability structure for this particular program, the State intends to conduct a year-long planning process in advance of pursuing any software implementation.
  • The State is engaging the designated Regional Health Information Organization (RHIO), CRISP Shared Services, to assist in rapidly planning the procurement and implementation of this solution.
  • The selected candidate will be responsible for project management of the RHIO completing requirements gathering, conducting landscape assessments and gap analyses, and providing a market overview for the State-Sponsored EHR. After this planning process and subsequent procurement of the EHR platform and implementation partner, the candidate will project manage the implementation process across voluntarily participating rural health providers in Rhode Island.

Responsibilities for this position shall include:
  • Active monitoring of contracts issued pertaining to EHR planning and implementation, ensuring adherence to timeline and contract terms for key milestones and deliverables
  • Complex cross-vendor and multi-stakeholder portfolio level management
  • Serve as a member of internal RHTP teams for coordination
  • Facilitate internal and external communications as necessary to disseminate opportunities to stakeholders
  • Provide a high level of subject expertise in enterprise software implementation
  • Collect and monitor outcomes data reporting from selected solution

Required Qualifications for Appointment
Knowledge, Skills, and Capacity:
  • Prior experience with EHR implementation or conversion
  • Prior experience project managing enterprise software
  • Deep knowledge of health IT clinical data standards and interoperability
  • Extremely organized and able to track input from an extensive list of stakeholders

Education and Experience
  • Education: Such as may have been gained through: Possession of a Bachelor’s degree from a college of recognized standing with specialization in a relevant field of Information Technology, Project Management, Healthcare Administration, a licensed health profession, or a closely related field; and
  • Experience: Such as may have been gained through considerable employment in a professional position with responsibilities related to information technology implementation, particularly in a healthcare setting.
  • Or, any combination of education and experience that shall be substantially equivalent to the above education and experience.

General Statement of Duties:
Serve as contract administrator for the Rural Health Transformation Project's Health IT initiative, specifically overseeing the client contract for the Rural Health Information Technology Fund (“HIT Fund”) administrator. This contract will issue more than $10M per year in funds to rural providers for support in health IT infrastructure, utilizing a scored application process alongside coordinated technical assistance. The selected candidate will be responsible for ensuring fiscal compliance for CMS grants in all areas and the vendor's adherence to scope of work requirements. 

Supervision:
Work under the direction and guidance of the State Health IT Coordinator and/or other senior program and policy leadership with considerable latitude for the exercise of initiative and independent judgment in the utilization for professional standards and techniques. 

Supervision Exercised:
No direct personnel supervised. Oversight of high-value contract, ensuring milestones and deliverables are produced professionally and in a timely manner.

SCOPE OF WORK
The HIT Fund will operate through three structured subaward categories: 1) equipment for currently billable services, 2) achievable and targeted software upgrades aligned with CMS Interoperability Framework goals, and 3) innovation and AI tools that do not otherwise fit with the other categories.
  1. For equipment grants, providers may request telehealth equipment, remote monitoring devices, or rated solutions tied to billable services and aligned with State-defined clinical priorities.
  2. For software-upgrade grants, funds will support enhancement to existing systems – not full conversions – such as population health modules, patient management applications, or other features that promote Interoperability Framework goals, with expectations for disbursement based on meeting implementation milestones.
  3. For innovation and AI grants, providers will propose concrete, evidence-supported tools such as scribe software or clinical-decision support modules with clearly defined outcomes that they will report back to the selected vendor and subsequently the State.
Awards will be made based on state-defined criteria and priorities such as alignment with the State’s RHTP goals; rurality and rural service commitment; HIT readiness and implementation capacity; interoperability and care coordination impact; and evidence of effectiveness, efficiency, and quality improvement. To prevent duplication, staff will review applications from other initiatives (e.g., Block Island and EMS equipment requests) before issuing awards. Where other initiatives fund specific equipment for defined programs, the HIT infrastructure grant will prioritize complementary or standalone technology needs for rural health that may not be addressed elsewhere.

Responsibilities for this position shall include:
  • Active monitoring of the contract issued to the selected HIT Fund administrator, ensuring adherence to timeline and contract terms for key milestones and deliverables
  • Process invoices and monitor all expenses for compliance with CMS grant requirements
  • Review provider applications to the fund for appropriateness and non-duplication across other RHTP programs
  • Serve as a member of internal RHTP teams for coordination

  • Provide high-level subject matter knowledge in applications of health information technology suitable for rural health providers, and associated implementation strategies
  • Collect and monitor outcomes data reporting from HIT Fund administrator and fund awardees

  • Experienced in healthcare administration

  • Able to coordinate numerous documentation requirements
  • Contract oversight and management
  • Team-based cross-project coordination

  • Comfortable with key health IT concepts
  • Knowledgeable about the concerns of rural residents and healthcare providers

  • Experience: Such as may have been gained through considerable employment in a professional position with responsibilities related to contract oversight, fiscal management, health policy, public health, public administration, program administration, or other relevant experience.

  • Must have a general understanding of public health, including healthcare finance, and healthcare delivery, and public health objectives.

Experience:

  • Extensive understanding with navigating the context of the ADA and Olmstead.

Job Summary:
The organization is seeking an Application Security Consultant to join the greater Information Security Team and help advance our enterprise application security program. This role will play a critical part in the design, build, and operation of security capabilities that protect the organization’s web, mobile, and cloud-native applications. The position requires broad application security experience across secure development practices, code analysis, cloud security, and production protection technologies.

As a member of the Cybersecurity Team, the consultant will execute and mature the application security architecture and framework across development, cloud, and production environments. The position will work directly with business application teams on secure design, code review oversight, release coordination, and production resilience. This role will formally represent the application security team in discussions involving new projects, architectures, and security control design, ensuring cybersecurity requirements are embedded early and consistently. Regular interaction with both technical and business personnel will be required to provide risk-based security analysis and recommendations that balance protection, performance, and delivery timelines.

The consultant will administer and optimize static code scanning solutions such as Checkmarx, ensure vulnerabilities are identified and remediated in alignment with OWASP Top Ten and broader industry risks, and collaborate closely with AWS engineering teams to secure Lambda functions and runtime resources. The role will also partner with change and release management to coordinate production code deployments from both security and reliability perspectives, while maintaining operational oversight of application-layer protection technologies.

  • Lead application security design and implementation across web, mobile, and AWS cloud-native services, including secure architecture reviews, AWS Lambda and runtime resource protection, and integration of security controls into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Administer and optimize static code scanning solutions such as Checkmarx, conduct vulnerability triage and remediation guidance aligned with OWASP Top Ten and broader application security risks, and validate security readiness prior to production release.
  • Manage and enhance application-layer protection technologies, including policy tuning, configuration updates, and detection improvements, ensuring protections remain effective without impacting performance or customer experience.
  • Coordinate closely with change and release management to align security controls with production deployment schedules, participate in go-live planning, and act in a Site Reliability Engineering capacity to ensure secure and stable releases.
  • Represent the application security team in project planning and architectural discussions, provide risk-based security analysis, and ensure cybersecurity requirements are embedded into design, development, and delivery decisions.
  • Provide structured security reporting, track remediation efforts, and support cross-functional project management activities to ensure application security initiatives are delivered on time and aligned with business objectives.
